newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to start T$30 bln textile venture in '98.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to start T$30 bln textile venture in '98.

text.p: A private textile association in Taiwan said on Monday it would begin construction for a T$30 billion polyester yarn joint venture involving 10 companies in 1998.
The Taiwan Association of Synthetic Stretch Yarn Industries said the venture, which includes textile giant Far Eastern Textile, would likely begin regular production in 1999.
The project's main product would be polyester drawn texturised yarn, a raw material for chemical fibre, the association said.
Spokesman Chiang declined to give details on production quantities.
"It is simply too early to tell," Chiang said.
"We are currently launching feasibility studies for the project to determine a site for the plants," association spokesman Chiang Cha-kung said by telephone.
"All the companies together will invest around T$30 billion, but this is only a rough estimate and the companies themselves can decide individually how much they want to participate," he said.
Other listed companies that have confirmed their participation were Hong Yi Fiber, Yin Jinn Industrial, Zig Sheng Industrial and Lan Fa Textile.
